questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That the academic opportunities were at least equal to that of my home university

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I found that the courses offered were very easy and taught me almost nothing compared to those offered at UCPH. The course catalogue was also very sparse, and I ended up not even taking any in my major (technically) which definitely was not part of my plan.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy, you get sent tons of information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Tons of emails, a tour and an orientation for exchange students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy, especially if you are there for a full year, since most offer 12-month leases, although may offer shorter if asked.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is A LOT cheaper than living on campus, and fairly easy to find a room in a newly built house.

Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I did most of it through the app, which worked alright and was fairly easy.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There are a lot of different offices you can email (or show up in person).

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Succesful, even though i technically didn't meet all the requirements, an email to the lecturer and one to the registration office did it.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't worry too much about prerequisites, just email the professor.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I found the courses were taught (mostly) very inefficiently, being required to do lots of work you didn't learn much from. (most of) the courses started at a very low level, also wasting valuable time. The course catalogue was also very sparse, where I only took one course, I actually had an interest in.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
Very low. Especially Fluid Mechanics had a very slow pace and very inefficient teaching methods. Quantum Chemistry also started off very slowly and picked up the pace a little bit towards the end, but was still far below the level I was used to at UCPH.
I also took a statistics course, which felt a little more like home, although the workload definetely didn't feel like 10 ECTS.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very inefficient. While the courses at UCPH puts a lot of weight on students solving exercise problems by themselves, this was not a very large part of the UC Merced courses, where exercise classes aren't a thing, and the problems are either walked through in class, painstakingly slow and/or left to the students to do at home, by themselves. Since the level was low I had no problems with this (except for the very large portion of lectures wasted), while I found the other students to be struggling vastly when faced with exercises.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Quantum Chemistry and Spectroscopy
Fluid Mechanics
Applied Statistics & Machine Learning

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Applied Statistics and Machine Learning. Maybe do a project if you can get credits for it, otherwise maybe check out graduate courses.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were almost no social events or social spots, you either need to join a fraternity/sorority and/or make great friends with people

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Little to none

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join a fraternity/sorority

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Yosemite is pretty obvious. The Bay Area is also nice and Hawai'i is amazing.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Fraternity/Sorority

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The tipping culture. It's always hard to know whether or not to tip, and how much, when you are a student on a budget, while essentialy being partially responsible for the workers salary

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: They were often pretty open and friendly

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Do not expect a comparable educational level.
Merced is a small town and UC Merced isn't known for it's social life.
Enjoy the opportunity of being on the west coast, go exploring another part of the world.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: none that i haven't mentioned

questions.answer: Experiencing a different culture

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Personal
